subject: Mobile Development
title: Windows Mobile's Early Lead
description: A quick win: understand Windows Mobile's Early Lead.

hook.text: Before Android existed, Microsoft had its own mobile OS running on dozens of phones.

buildup.text: Windows Mobile put a tiny Start menu on a phone screen. It felt like a shrunken PC.

discovery.text: Business users loved it. Exchange email sync worked better than any competitor.

twist.text: The interface needed a stylus for tiny buttons. Fingers were too big to tap accurately.

climax.text: When the iPhone arrived with finger-friendly touch, Windows Mobile looked obsolete overnight.

punchline.text: Shrinking Windows to a phone never worked.

quiz.question: Why did Windows Mobile struggle after the iPhone?
options: Its interface required a stylus, not fingers
